title: The caravan comes home, its stores lighter and its pilgrims changed. Word has run ahead of the camels, and crowds gather at Ishbīliya to welcome a ruler who stood before the Kaʿba. From this day the Emperor bears the title Ḥājjī, earned and not granted. Let it be known: Makka and back, by the grace of Allāh

effects.modifier: Blessings of the Ḥajj, 5 years: +5% clergy satisfaction equilibrium
effects.trait: Ḥājjī: +0.1 prestige and +0.1 legitimacy a month

source: Trent's screenshot of the event, 20 February 1392

title: The empire turns to the Atlantic. Beside Khayr al-Dīn's voyage down the African coast toward Mali, two more expeditions set out with new explorers: one to chart the sea of the Azores, the other to Madeira

expeditions: the African coast to Mali (Khayr al-Dīn al-Jayyānī, 1391)
data.explorers: new explorers for the Azores and Madeira; names await a save
data.history: the Azores and Madeira were known to Genoese and Portuguese sailors by the mid-fourteenth century, but not settled until the 1420s; Arab geographers had written of islands in the western Ocean

title: A year after Aiman's death the Emperor meets grief as he always has, with innovation. Banking and moneylending are formalised in the empire and made more permissive: al-Andalus embraces the new institution of banking, born among the Genoese

data.spread: 20.62% of the realm's locations when embraced
